issues.title: add_business_days counts Saturday as business day (weekday()<6 instead of <5), causing Friday express to promise Saturday delivery

findings.summary: Friday express orders were promised Saturday delivery (e.g., 2026-10-23 -> 2026-10-24) causing courier booking failures with no weekend slots. H1 confirmed as root cause off-by-one. Patch fixes delivery.py:22 and is verified by test_express_from_friday_skips_weekend with no regressions.

report.diff:
--- a/shipping/delivery.py
+++ b/shipping/delivery.py
@@ -19,7 +19,7 @@
     current, added = start, 0
     while added < days:
         current += timedelta(days=1)
-        if current.weekday() < 6 and current not in holidays(current.year):
+        if current.weekday() < 5 and current not in holidays(current.year):
             added += 1
     return current
 
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_regression_friday_express.py
@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+from datetime import date
+from shipping.delivery import estimate_delivery, is_business_day
+
+def test_express_from_friday_skips_weekend():
+    # 2026-10-23 is a Friday; express (1 business day) must land Monday 2026-10-26,
+    # not Saturday 2026-10-24 (carrier has no weekend slots).
+    promised = estimate_delivery(date(2026, 10, 23), "express")
+    assert promised == date(2026, 10, 26)
+    assert is_business_day(promised)

second_opinion.summary: Patch fixes root cause off-by-one at delivery.py:22 (<6 -> <5) aligning add_business_days with is_business_day and carrier weekend closure. Evidence chain from code inconsistency to logs to failing regression test directly supports H1, and fix is verified with no regressions.

hypotheses.note: Code diff <6 vs <5 proves Saturday counted as business day; logs show Friday 2026-10-23 express promised Saturday 2026-10-24 and carrier ValueError on same date; regression test reproduction matches.
